interface.title: Generations Study — Data Dashboard
interface.field: Epidemiology / cohort studies (Breast Cancer Now Generations Study)
interface.stage_of_work: Data exploration, quality checks and cohort definition before analysis; making the descriptive Table 1
interface.what_it_is_for: A browser-only dashboard where a researcher loads participant-level JSON data with its JSON Schema, looks at each variable's distribution and missingness, compares groups, builds an AND/OR filtered cohort with a live attrition flow, and exports a Table 1 as CSV.

data.note: I uploaded synthetic_data.json (40 records) with DerivedVariables_Schema.json, giving 17 variables in 5 groups (Demographics, Anthropometry, Reproductive, Lifestyle, Medical History; the sidebar's extra 'Data' chip holds the TCode ID). Adding synthetic_cancer_data.json and CancerSummary_Schema.json was refused with the alert 'Duplicate TCode "GS000007" found in "synthetic_cancer_data.json". Files with multiple rows per participant are not currently supported'. This is the app's documented behaviour (the README says files with duplicate TCodes are rejected); the cause was the hand-written test file, which deliberately put two records on GS000007. A successful multi-file join was therefore not shown, and all later work used the main dataset only.

features.name: Stratifiable Table 1 with CSV export
features.general: Make a descriptive-statistics table for the current subset (mean (SD) for continuous variables, n (%) for categorical ones, separate percentages for missing and 'not applicable'), optionally split into columns by a grouping variable, and export the overall table as CSV. Known limits: the split view shows only the first two groups by code, and the CSV holds only the overall column
features.specific: Descriptive Statistics (n=…) table with legend, a Stratify by dropdown (None or a categorical variable), Generate, and Export CSV (table1.csv with Variable, Type, Summary, Null %, NA Sentinel %, Sentinel value). Stratified view renders only the first two strata by sorted code (not the largest two); the CSV has no stratum columns, and its categorical summaries are raw codes and counts (e.g. '1:4; 4:1'), not labels and percentages

Press Generate
Read the All column and the first two per-stratum columns
Press Export CSV (overall summary only)
